definitions.explanation: A humble expression meaning to meet or see someone, used when referring to meeting someone of higher status.

examples.japanese: お{目|め}に{掛|か}かれて{光栄|こうえい}です。
examples.english: It's an honor to meet you.

examples.japanese: {先日|せんじつ}お{目|め}に{掛|か}かった{方|かた}
examples.english: The person I met the other day.

examples.japanese: またお{目|め}に{掛|か}かりたいです。
examples.english: I would like to meet you again.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}にお{目|め}に{掛|か}かる{機会|きかい}をいただき、{大変|たいへん}{嬉|うれ}しく{存|ぞん}じます。
examples.english: I am very pleased to have been given the opportunity to meet the company president.
examples.notes: [Note: 存じます is humble form of 思います]

notes:
お{目|め}に{掛|か}かる is a humble verb for meeting someone.

FORMALITY:
- Very formal/humble expression
- Used in business and formal situations
- Shows respect to the person you are meeting

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- お{目|め}に{掛|か}かる: to meet (humble)
- {会|あ}う: to meet (neutral)
- お{会|あ}いする: to meet (polite)
- {拝見|はいけん}する: to see (humble, for things)

CONJUGATION:
- お{目|め}に{掛|か}かります (polite)
- お{目|め}に{掛|か}かれて (te-form)
- お{目|め}に{掛|か}かった (past)
